final_message:
I couldn't reproduce the bug, so I haven't changed anything. `median([1, 2, 3, 4])` returns `2.5` with the code in `src/stats_utils.py`.

The function sorts the input. For an even count it averages the two middle values, so `(2 + 3) / 2 = 2.5`. For an odd count it returns the middle value.

The users may be running a different version than this checkout, such as an older release or an installed copy of the package. They could also be calling some other `median`, for example one that picks the upper middle element, `s[n // 2]`, which would give `3`.

My grep for other uses of `median` in the repo failed on a shell glob error, so I haven't ruled out a second implementation elsewhere. I can re-run it, or you can ask the users which version they have and how they call it.
